name: AArk Granting Program
summary: Seed grants for newly launched ex situ amphibian rescue programmes for species assessed as needing rescue, plus small workshop grants and emergency grants through the year.

amount.note: Program grants: up to US$7,000 in the first year, with smaller sums in years 2 and 3

reporting: Progress reports at 6, 12, 24 and 36 months after the programme starts, as set out in the MOU.

eligibility.rule: Program grants: species assessed as needing ex situ rescue or research by a Conservation Needs Assessment
Program grants: the ex situ rescue project is newly launched
Workshop grants: partial funding already secured and active in an amphibian conservation project
Workshop grants: not a general education or awareness programme
Emergency grants: an urgent, unforeseen threat to an amphibian rescue population
Funding is administered through an eligible institution or organization

documents: Two endorsement letters from unrelated conservation leaders
Project budget distinguishing AArk and other funds

status.quote: Applications for 2026 grants cycle are now closed - stay tuned for the 2027 cycle!

geography.quote: We welcome applications from all countries, especially those that have established National Programs.

access.quote: We welcome applications from all countries, especially those that have established National Programs.

window.quote: Applications for 2026 grants cycle are now closed - stay tuned for the 2027 cycle!

amount.quote: Funded programs will receive up to US$7,000 in the first year. Additional funds will be available for year 2 (up to US$5,000) and year 3 (up to US$3,000) if projects have met their stated objectives

applicant_types.quote: Amphibian Ark can provide funding to NGOs and, in some cases, government institutions involved in amphibian conservation.

reporting.quote: Send a progress report 6, 12, 24, and 36 months after the program starts as per the MOU.

effort.quote: Applicants must still submit the form

eligibility.quote: Species must have been assessed as in need of ex situ rescue or research by a Conservation Needs Assessment.
This application is for newly-launched ex situ rescue projects
Applicants must have already secured partial funding and be actively involved in an amphibian conservation project.
General education and awareness programs are not eligible.
Emergency Grants are intended for urgent, unforeseen situations that threaten the survival of amphibian rescue populations.
Funding must be administered through an eligible institution or organization.

after_award.quote: A progress report and photos 6 and 12 months after funding is received.

documents.quote: Please provide a timeline of work, ideally beyond the granting period.

One letter of institutional support. This letter must verify that the institution a) is aware that the applicant is proposing this project, and b) will provide the necessary resources, time, and space to complete the proposed work for the duration of the project. - Two letters of endorsement from recognized conservation leaders at organizations unrelated to this project.
Submit a budget, with distinction between funds requested from Amphibian Ark and other sources.
